headline: Oracle Says OpenAI Commitment Is Fully Financed
deck: The company’s funding assertion is paired with a coming rack handover, site milestones and an investment-cycle fundraising cap.
body: Oracle said in a 20 November statement that it had secured all the funding needed to fulfil its contract with OpenAI [E1]. Investing.com reported that Oracle characterized ongoing private supplier discussions as optional, and Oracle said its ability to deliver on the contract did not depend on them [E10][E2]. The company described the handover of Nvidia Vera Rubin racks in its data halls as on track for the coming weeks [E3].

At its investor day, Oracle said it expected total revenue to grow at a compound annual rate of more than 35% from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2030, reaching at least $225 billion in fiscal 2030, alongside strong profitability and free-cash-flow generation across its three business models [E4].

Oracle said it would limit additional capital-markets funding for its fiscal 2027–2030 investment cycle to $20 billion, currently expected as $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in gross debt; the incremental requirement excludes refinancing of existing debt and is in addition to a $20 billion at-the-market equity raise completed in fiscal 2027’s first quarter [E5]. Vendor financing, customer-provided hardware and customer prepayments are expected to reduce upfront cash requirements, the company said [E6].

Oracle entered an underwriting agreement with BofA Securities on 2 November to issue and sell 86,206,897 common shares; the offering closed on 4 November [E7]. It said the proceeds could be used for general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure, debt repayment, investments or acquisitions, dividends and share repurchases [E8]. Its notes offering was made under a registration statement and a related preliminary prospectus supplement dated 2 November [E9].

Investing.com reported that Oracle’s statement arrived amid broader scrutiny of how technology providers finance capital expenditure exceeding current operating cash flows [E10]. It also reported that construction at Oracle’s Abilene campus was nearing completion and that its next gigawatt-scale site in Shackelford had obtained full permitting [E11].

This paper’s 25 August coverage reported that OpenAI planned to begin deploying Jalapeño within its compute infrastructure [E12]. Oracle’s new statement concerns funding for its contract with OpenAI and a coming Vera Rubin rack handover [E1][E3].
